name: Firebase Auth
summary: Firebase Authentication is a ready-made login system from Google that handles sign-up, sign-in, and password resets for you.

free_plan_covers.note: Email/password and social sign-in are free up to 50,000 monthly active users on the Spark plan, more than a small app needs.

first_paid_usd_month.note: No flat monthly fee; it is pay-as-you-go past the free user quota. Phone/SMS sign-in has no free quota and needs the paid plan.

portability.note: Firebase can export users and password hashes for reimport elsewhere, but the hash format needs project-specific parameters.

mobile_sdk.note: Official SDKs cover iOS, Android, and Flutter; React Native works through a widely used community package instead.

prebuilt_ui.note: FirebaseUI provides official, actively maintained sign-in and sign-up screens for web, iOS, and Android.

setup.step: Create a Firebase project at the Firebase console.
Register a web app in the project to get your Firebase config values.
Install the Firebase SDK in your Next.js app.
In the console, open Authentication and enable the sign-in methods you want; all are off by default.
Add the Firebase config values to your app. Firebase's docs do not require environment variables, but NEXT_PUBLIC_ names are a common Next.js convention.

builder_notes: Every sign-in provider is off by default and must be explicitly enabled in the Firebase console before users can use it.
The web config values (apiKey, etc.) are safe for browser code; they are not secret. Never send an Admin SDK service account key to the browser.
Firebase Auth only checks identity; pair it with Firestore Security Rules using request.auth.uid to actually restrict data access.
